content: Dual-write/partial-write risk when retrofitting transactions onto existing multi-statement persistence: each independent autocommit statement is its own implicit transaction, so a crash between statements leaves partial state. Fix for single-DB multi-statement writes is a real explicit transaction (one connection, BEGIN/COMMIT), not a distributed saga/outbox (those solve cross-service/cross-broker dual-writes, not single-Postgres multi-statement writes). A separate external system (e.g. a checkpointer or cache) written outside that transaction is still a genuine dual-write even if it shares the same underlying database, because it uses a separate connection/transaction.
